title: Switch off a named rotary isolator and padlock its handle at OFF
instruction: Switch off isolator Q1, the one with the yellow nameplate: turn its handle a quarter turn anticlockwise, as you face it, from ON (pointing up) to OFF (pointing left). Then pull the red padlock slide down out of the grip by its tab at the grip's tip, put your padlock's shackle through the hole in the tab and snap it shut. Do not turn isolator Q2, the one with the white nameplate.
context: Before work on a machine, each worker switches its local isolator OFF and padlocks it there. Switching off the wrong isolator, or leaving the right one OFF but not padlocked, lets someone switch the machine back on while a person is working on it.
setup: Positions are measured forward from the line joining the two arm bases (61 cm apart), left or right of their midline as seen from behind the robot, and up from the table top. Backboard: a plywood board (1.8 cm thick, 40 cm wide, 33 cm tall) stands on the table on two 4 cm wide feet, its front face 40 cm in front of the bases, spanning 32 cm right to 8 cm left of the midline. Isolators: two small light-grey plastic enclosures (10 cm wide, 15 cm tall, 9 cm deep) are fixed to the board, their fronts 31 cm in front of the bases and their centres 20.5 cm above the table: Q1 on the midline and Q2 24 cm right of it. Each holds an ABB OT16F3 3-pole 16 A switch-disconnector worked by an ABB OHB45J6 black pistol handle on the enclosure's front, its axis at the enclosure's centre (round base 67 mm across; handle 45 mm deep; grip 38 mm wide, 44 mm from the axis to its tip). ON is the grip pointing up; OFF is the grip pointing left, a quarter turn anticlockwise as you face the handle; both start ON. Each handle has ABB's red padlock slide in its grip: a red stripe (6 x 13 mm) flush along the grip's lower edge (at OFF) from 20 mm out from the axis to the grip's tip, ending at the tip in a red finger tab (6 mm thick, 17 mm deep) that shows 16 mm below the grip. At OFF the slide pulls straight down 32 mm by the finger tab: its tail then drops into a slot in the handle's fixed base, and an 8.5 mm square hole in the tab (its axis along the grip) shows 17 mm below the grip's outer half, 37.5 mm in front of the enclosure, 39 mm out from the axis along the grip and 40 mm below it. At any other angle the slide cannot be pulled out. Nameplates: an engraved two-ply laminate plate (86 x 30 mm) on each enclosure's front, centred 5.4 cm above the axis, with 20 mm black letters: Q1 on yellow, Q2 on white. Padlock: a Master Lock 410 Zenex safety padlock (purple, 410PRP; body 38 x 45 x 19 mm, 6.35 mm steel shackle with 38 mm vertical and 19 mm horizontal clearance; 0.10 kg), open (shackle popped out 16 mm, key in the cylinder), lies flat (its labelled faces up and down) on a grey plastic post (1.6 x 1.4 cm, 15.6 cm tall, on a 6 x 6 x 1 cm foot) that supports the shackle half of its body: body centre 25 cm in front of the bases, 17 cm left of the midline and 16.5 cm above the table, shackle pointing right (toward the midline), short leg on the far side (away from the robot). Both arms start at the ready pose with their grippers open. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Score 0 if, at any time, Q2's handle turns 10 degrees or more, or Q1's handle, after reaching OFF, goes back more than 30 degrees toward ON before the padlock is shut. Otherwise the score is the highest level reached: 0.25 if Q1's handle has turned 10 degrees or more from ON toward OFF; 0.5 if it reaches OFF (within 5 degrees of its stop, pointing left); 0.75 if, with Q1 at OFF and its slide pulled out (within 3 mm of fully out), the padlock's short leg also passes through the hole in the slide's tab; 1.0 if the padlock is also shut (shackle latched) through the hole and the after-release check passes. Dropping the padlock is not penalised by itself. After-release check, done once both grippers have been at least 6 cm from the padlock for 2 s: push the slide's finger tab up into the grip with a spring scale at 10 N and keep pushing; after 2 s also turn the handle toward ON with 2 N m (a spring scale hooked at the grip's tip, 44 mm from the axis, pulling 45 N) for 2 s. Pass if the handle stays within 20 degrees of OFF and the shackle is still through the hole; if not, the score is 0.75. Angles are read from a front photo with a protractor template.
reset_notes: Open the padlock with its key and take it off the slide; push Q1's red slide back into the handle and turn the handle back to ON (pointing up); check Q2 is ON; lay the open padlock flat back on its post (left of Q1) with its shackle toward the midline and its short leg on the far side. About 1 minute.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies on joints, arms with the station's i2rt gains. Lock chain is geometry: the slide's tail drops into the base's slot only at OFF and stops the handle; a shackle in the tab's hole meets the grip if the slide is pushed in. Slide follows ABB's leaflet but its inside, straight pull, one 8.5 mm hole (ABB: up to 3 locks) and enlarged finger tab are ours. Torque 0.4 N m (ABB: 1 N m) for the soft-gain arm; no snap action; box colliders. Details in README.
